BURHAN:v4p392/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p392/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p392/r9.claim: Hope or apprehension expressed by لعل can belong to the addressee or another party: the first example hopes Pharaoh will follow, and the second has Moses and Aaron hoping he will heed them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r4.claim: Soft speech is intrinsic to prophetic preaching and reform, reflecting a teacher's affection and a well-wisher's sympathy, rather than weakness before Pharaoh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r4.anchor: softness is the nature of every preaching effort

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r5.claim: Prophets do not impose themselves arrogantly; that manner belongs to worldly leaders and underlies contemporary satanic propaganda.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r5.anchor: Imposing one’s self in an arrogant way is the trait of leaders who have become slaves of this world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r6.claim: The purpose of prophetic instruction is to remind people and awaken fear of God; indifferent people may return to guidance when reminded.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r6.anchor: express the purpose of the teaching and preaching of prophets: reminding people and making them fear God

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.claim: Although Pharaoh had greatly transgressed, the command to address him gently shows how important method and tone are to successful religious preaching.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.anchor: 24 ve 43. âyetlerde Firavun’a uyarıcı gönderilme gerekçesi olarak “onun sınırı çok aştığı” ifade edildiği halde 44. âyette “Yine de ona söyleyeceklerinizi yumuşak bir üslûpla söyleyiniz

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r8.claim: The gentle speech resembles Moses' offer to Pharaoh to purify himself and be guided to his Lord; presenting it as a question, counsel, and offer is rhetorically delicate given its great benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r8.anchor: والقول اللين هو مثل ما في النازعات هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى وهذا من لطيف الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r9.claim: One interpretation is that they offered Pharaoh everlasting youth, an unassailable kingdom, and continued bodily pleasures until death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r9.anchor: وقيل: عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده وملكا لا ينزع منه إلا بالموت وأن يبقى له لذة المطعم والمشرب والمنكح إلى حين موته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r10.claim: Another interpretation says not to confront Pharaoh with what he dislikes, but to speak gently because he had raised Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r10.anchor: وقيل: لا تجبهاه بما يكره وألطفا له في القول لما له من حق تربية موسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r11.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r11.claim: One view says they should address Pharaoh by one of his four honorific kunyas: Abū Murrah, Abū Muṣʿab, Abū al-Walīd, or Abū al-ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r11.anchor: وقيل: كنياه وهو ذو الكنى الأربع أبو مرة، وأبو مصعب، وأبو الوليد، وأبو العباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r12.claim: Another view identifies the gentle speech as lā ilāha illā Allāh, whose gentleness lies in its ease on the tongue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r12.anchor: وقيل: القول اللين لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، ولينها خفتها على اللسان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r13.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says they should tell Pharaoh he has a Lord and an afterlife, with Paradise for faith and Fire for unbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو قولهما إن لك ربا وإن لك معادا وإن بين يديك جنة ونارا فآمن بالله يدخلك الجنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r14.claim: One view says God ordered Moses and Aaron to present promises before threats, as in a poet's instruction to start with a promise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r14.anchor: وقيل: أمرهما تعالى أن يقدما المواعيد على الوعيد كما قال الشاعر: أقدم بالوعد قبل الوعيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r15.claim: A report says Pharaoh consulted Āsiyah after Moses and Aaron's offer; she advised acceptance, but Hāmān warned that Pharaoh would become owned instead of master and worshipper instead of lord, so he refused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r15.anchor: فشاور هامان وكان لا يبت أمرا دون رأيه، فقال له: كنت أعتقد أنك ذو عقل تكون مالكا فتصير مملوكا وربا فتصير مربوبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r16.claim: The hope expressed by laʿalla belongs to Moses and Aaron, since hope is impossible for God; they are told to act hopefully and not despair of success.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r16.anchor: والترجي بالنسبة لهما إذ هو مستحيل وقوعه من الله تعالى أي اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r17.claim: God sent them despite knowing Pharaoh would not believe in order to establish proof and remove his excuse, as the cited verse says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r17.anchor: وفائدة إرسالهما مع علمه تعالى أنه لا يؤمن إقامة الحجة عليه وإزالة المعذرة كما قال تعالى: ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r1.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the gentle speech as the full message, from the instruction to approach Pharaoh through the greeting to followers of guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r1.anchor: وهو فأتياه فقولا إنا رسولا ربك- إلى قوله- والسلام على من اتبع الهدى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r2.speaker: أبو معاذ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r2.claim: Abu Muadh glosses the command as simply saying a gentle word.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r3.claim: Al-Farra reads laʿalla purposively as meaning so that Pharaoh may remember or fear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء لعل هنا بمعنى كي أي كي يتذكر أو يخشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r4.claim: An alternative takes laʿalla as a question: will Pharaoh remember or fear?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r4.anchor: وقيل: لعل هنا استفهام أي هل يتذكر أو يخشى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers laʿalla in its ordinary sense of hope relative to human speakers; the wording shows Moses was not doubtful about God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r5.anchor: والصحيح أنها على بابها من الترجي وذلك بالنسبة إلى البشر وفي قوله لعله يتذكر أو يخشى دلالة على أنه لم يكن شاكا في الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r6.claim: A report says Pharaoh once prostrated at the Nile after it stopped, then hoped its following his horse would remind him of God's forbearance and generosity and warn him of punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r6.anchor: يتذكر حاله حين احتبس النيل فسار إلى شاطئه وأبعد وخر ساجدا لله راغبا أن لا يخجله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says remembrance means reflection that leads Pharaoh to fairness and submission to truth, while fear means fearing the brothers' warning may be true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p337/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أي يتذكر ويتأمل فيبذل النصفة من نفسه والإذعان للحق أو يخشى أن يكون الأمر كما يصفان

AKHFASH:v2p443/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p443/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p443/r7.claim: لعل here expresses purpose, like لنتغدى or حتى نتغدى; likewise, لعلك تأخذ أجرك means لتأخذه.
AKHFASH:v2p443/r7.anchor: وقال {لعله يتذكر} نحو قول الرجل لصاحبه: "افرع لعلنا نتغدى" والمعنى: "لنتغدى" و"حتى نتغدى". وتقول للرجل: "اعمل عملك لعلك تأخذ أجرك" أي: لتأخذه.

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh marvels that God is gentle toward one claiming divinity, asking how gentle He is toward one who claims to be His servant.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r1.anchor: رفقك بمن يدعي العبودية. وتدل على أن في القرآن مجازا؛

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r2.claim: The passage shows that the Quran uses metaphor: describing speech as gentle is figurative and highly eloquent.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r2.anchor: وتدل على أن في القرآن مجازا؛ لأن اللين في صفة الكلام مجاز، وهو هاهنا في غاية الفصاحة.

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r3.claim: A servant's act originates from the servant; if God created it, gentleness and other actions would be alike, and the relevant issue would be God's creating faith in Pharaoh.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن فعل العبد حادث من جهته؛ إذ لو كان خلقا لله تعالى لكان الرفق وغيره سواء، وكان المعتبر خلق الله فيه الإيمان

JISHUMI:v7p4672/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r4.claim: The word laʿalla shows that God intended Pharaoh and his people to remember, against the determinists.
JISHUMI:v7p4672/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: لعله أنه أراد منهم التذكر خلاف قول المجبرة.

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r1.speaker: Bḍ, Z
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r1.claim: Some commentators connect the gentle address with the invitation in 79:18–19 to be purified and guided to the Lord.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r1.anchor: According to some commentators, the command here is similar to the words God tells Moses to speak to Pharaoh in 79:18–19

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r2.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r2.claim: “Gently” may mean “a gentle word,” understood by some as the shahādah, “There is no god but God.”

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r3.claim: The command can be taken generally as requiring Moses to communicate God’s message to Pharaoh gently.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r3.anchor: Gently is also seen as a general command to Moses to communicate the message to Pharaoh in a gentle manner (IK)

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī argues that harsh admonition makes tyrants more obstinate and proud, whereas gentleness might let Pharaoh respond positively.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r4.anchor: it is customary for tyrants, when they are admonished harshly, to increase in their obstinacy and pride

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r5.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r5.claim: Since Pharaoh raised Moses, al-Rāzī says gentleness was fitting in recognition of caregivers’ rights.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r5.anchor: since Moses was brought up by Pharaoh, it was only fitting that Moses be gentle with him

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r6.speaker: JJ, IK
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r6.claim: “Remember” means to heed Pharaoh’s warning or to turn away from his misguidance.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r6.anchor: Remember here refers to Pharaoh’s taking heed of the warning given to him (JJ) and turning away from his misguidance (IK)

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r7.speaker: JJ, IK
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r7.claim: “Fear” means that Pharaoh would fear God and return to Him, or become obedient to Him.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r7.anchor: fear is understood to mean that Pharaoh would be fearful of God, return to Him (JJ), and be obedient toward Him (IK)

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r8.claim: Laʿalla conveys “perhaps,” “hopefully,” or “it might be that.”

STUDYQURAN:20:44/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r9.speaker: JJ, R
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r9.claim: The hopeful “perhaps” is for Moses and Aaron, who cannot know the result of their warning but are to hope Pharaoh will heed it or fear God.
STUDYQURAN:20:44/r9.anchor: haply is said for the benefit of Moses and Aaron (JJ), who could not know the outcome of delivering God’s warning

TAB-FULL:v16p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p75/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v16p75/r1.claim: Al-Tabari explains that Moses and Aaron were to speak gently to Pharaoh; al-Suddi says this means addressing him by his kunya.
TAB-FULL:v16p75/r1.anchor: عن السدي: {فقولا له قولا لينا} [طه: 44] قال: كنياه

TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas takes laʿalla here as a question: will Pharaoh reflect and return, or fear God and desist? Al-Tabari says this view has a sound basis.
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} [طه: 44] يقول: هل يتذكر أو يخشى

TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r2.claim: Another view takes laʿalla as ‘so that’: Moses and Aaron should summon and admonish Pharaoh in order that he reflect or fear; al-Tabari accepts both interpretations as valid.
TAB-FULL:v16p75#2/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى لعل ههنا كي

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.claim: God renews the command to both messengers, matching the previous joint address and prohibition against slackening.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.anchor: جمعهما في الأمر ثانيا فخاطب موسى وهارون معا وكذلك في النهي الذي قبله

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.claim: Gentle speech forbids harsh and violent treatment and is one of the essential etiquettes of inviting people to faith.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.anchor: المنع من أن يكلماه بخشونة وعنف وهو من أوجب آداب الدعوة

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r13.claim: The hope of Pharaoh's reflection or fear is voiced from within the dialogue, not because God is uncertain about what will happen.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r13.anchor: رجاء لتذكره أو خشيته وهو قائم بمقام المحاورة لا به تعالى العالم بما سيكون

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r14.claim: Remembrance is accepting the reminder, its proof, and belief in it; fear precedes acceptance, so the phrase means he may believe or approach belief and answer them.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r14.anchor: والتذكر مطاوعة التذكير فيكون قبولا والتزاما لما تقتضيه حجة المذكر وإيمانه به

TABRISI:20:40-44/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:40-44/r20.claim: Ibn Abbas says to deal gently with Pharaoh in the invitation and not speak harshly.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r20.anchor: أي ارفقا به في الدعاء والقول ولا تغلظا له في ذلك عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:20:40-44/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r21.speaker: السدي وعكرمة
TABRISI:20:40-44/r21.claim: Al-Suddi and Ikrima interpret gentle speech as addressing Pharaoh by a kunya; views name Abu al-Walid, Abu al-Abbas, or Abu Marra.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r21.anchor: معناه كنياه عن السدي وعكرمة وكنيته أبو الوليد

TABRISI:20:40-44/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r22.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:20:40-44/r22.claim: Muqatil identifies gentle speech with Moses' invitation to be purified and guided to his Lord, the wording quoted in 79:18–19.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r22.anchor: وقيل: إن القول اللين هو هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى عن مقاتل

TABRISI:20:40-44/r23.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r23.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:40-44/r23.claim: Another account says Moses offered Pharaoh Islam in exchange for lasting youth, kingship, bodily pleasures until death, and Paradise afterward; Pharaoh liked it but waited for Haman's counsel.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r23.anchor: تسلم وتؤمن برب العالمين على أن لك شبابك فلا تهرم

TABRISI:20:44/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r1.speaker: هامان
TABRISI:20:44/r1.claim: Haman rebukes Pharaoh for wanting to move from being a lord to a subject and from being worshipped to worshipping, turning him away from accepting Moses' invitation.
TABRISI:20:44/r1.anchor: قد كنت أرى أن لك عقلا وأن لك رأيا

TABRISI:20:44/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r2.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
TABRISI:20:44/r2.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh remarks that if this is the gentleness shown to someone claiming divinity, one should consider the gentleness due to someone claiming servitude.
TABRISI:20:44/r2.anchor: هذا رفقك بمن يدعي الربوبية فكيف رفقك بمن يدعي العبودية

TABRISI:20:44/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:44/r3.claim: The brothers are to call Pharaoh with hope that he will remember or fear, rather than despairing of his success; this posture is more effective in summoning him to truth.
TABRISI:20:44/r3.anchor: ادعواه على الرجاء والطمع لا على اليأس من فلاحه

TABRISI:20:44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:20:44/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj, following Sibawayh, explains the wording as 'go with your hope and expectation'; God knows the outcome, but messengers are sent hoping people accept.
TABRISI:20:44/r4.anchor: والمعنى في هذا عند سيبويه اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما

TABRISI:20:44/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:44/r5.claim: The mission's purpose is that Pharaoh recall God's lordship and his own servitude, and fear the punishment and warning.
TABRISI:20:44/r5.anchor: والمراد بيان الغرض بالبعثة أي ليتذكر ما أغفل عنه

TABRISI:20:44/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:44/r6.claim: Gentleness in calling people to God, commanding right, and forbidding wrong helps them accept the message and keeps them from recoiling.
TABRISI:20:44/r6.anchor: يرفق في الدعاء إلى الله وفي الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r1.claim: One explanation from Ibn Abbas, also held by ʿIkrima and al-Suddī, is that Moses and Aaron should address Pharaoh by a kunya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r1.anchor: {فقولا له قولا لينا} ذكر ابن عباس فيه قولين: أحدهما: (كنياه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r2.claim: Reported kunyas for Pharaoh are Abū al-ʿAbbās, Abū al-Walīd, and Abū Murra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r2.anchor: واختلفوا في كنيته فقيل: أبو العباس، وأبو الوليد، وأبو مرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r3.claim: Another report describes Moses offering Pharaoh belief and worship in exchange for lasting youth, kingdom, pleasures, and eventual entry to Paradise.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، وأبي صالح السدي عن أبي مالك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r4.claim: Muqātil identifies the gentle words with the invitation to purify himself and accept guidance in 79:18–19.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#3/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني بالقول اللين: {فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى (18)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r1.claim: The messengers invite Pharaoh with hope rather than certainty of success; earnest hope makes their call to truth more compelling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r1.anchor: {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} أي: ادعوه على الرجاء والطمع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq, explaining Sibawayh, says God speaks in terms humans understand: Moses and Aaron act in hope though God knows the outcome, since prophets do not know the unseen.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r2.anchor: والمعنى في هذا عند سيبويه: اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq adds that divine foreknowledge cannot itself establish the human proof; otherwise sending messengers would serve no purpose.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r3.anchor: وليس علم الله بما سيكون يجب به الحجة على الآدميين، ولو كان ذلك لم يكن في الرسل فائدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī reports al-Farrāʾ’s reading of laʿalla as “so that,” in keeping with the two messengers’ expectation and course of action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p409/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: (مذهب الفراء في {لعله يتذكر} كي يتذكر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r1.claim: They should address Pharaoh by his kunya and promise faith's blessings: wealth, a long healthy life, and an eventual destination in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r1.anchor: كنياه وعداه على الإيمان نعيما وعمرا طويلا في صحة، ومصيرا إلى الجنة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r2.claim: 'Perhaps' reflects Moses and Aaron's hope: they go hoping for this, although God already knows Pharaoh's outcome.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:44-47/r2.anchor: يعود إلى حال موسى وهارون. أي: اذهبا أنتما على رجائكما وطمعكما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r4.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r4.claim: Some Kufans say gentle speech means addressing Pharaoh by his kunya.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r5.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r5.claim: Al-Suddī treats the connective as redundant: perhaps Pharaoh will remember and fear God.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r5.anchor: وتفسير السدي أن الألف هاهنا صلة يقول: لعله يذكر ويخشى الله.

QASHANI:20:41-44/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:41-44/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:41-44/r3.claim: The heart and intellect should gently invite the soul to submit to divine command and follow the law, so that it may soften and obey.
QASHANI:20:41-44/r3.anchor: { فقولا له قولا لينا } بالرفق والمداراة في دعوتها إلى الاستسلام لأمر الحق

BURHAN:v4p390/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p390/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p390/r8.claim: Laalla expresses hope for a desired outcome or apprehension of an unwanted one; these states cannot literally describe God, since they imply uncertainty.
BURHAN:v4p390/r8.anchor: لعل تجيء لمعان الاول للترجي في المحبوب

BURHAN:v4p390/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p390/r9.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v4p390/r9.claim: Sibawayh shifts the hope to Moses and Aaron: they are to hope Pharaoh may remember or fear, since they could not yet know that he would not believe.

BURHAN:v4p56/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p56/r5.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
BURHAN:v4p56/r5.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh take لعله in its ordinary sense of hope from Moses and Aaron's perspective, since God already knows Pharaoh's outcome; this is better than al-Farra's causal reading.
BURHAN:v4p56/r5.anchor: اذهبا إلى رجائكما وطمعكما لعله يتذكر عندكما

BURHAN:v4p56/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p56/r6.speaker: الفراء
BURHAN:v4p56/r6.claim: Al-Farra interprets لعله as causal, but the author says this takes the wording out of its ordinary function.
BURHAN:v4p56/r6.anchor: وهذا أحسن من قول الفراء إنها تعليلة أي يتذكر لما فيه من إخراج اللفظ عن موضعه

BURHAN:v4p158/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p158/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p158/r1.claim: Possible events are certain in God's knowledge but doubtful to creatures, so Qur'anic expressions of certainty or hope reflect the relevant perspective.
BURHAN:v4p158/r1.anchor: والوجه في استعمال هذه الالفاظ أن الامور الممكنة لما كان الخلق يشكون فيها

BURHAN:v4p158/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p158/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p158/r2.claim: God knew Pharaoh would not heed the warning, but the wording presents Moses and Aaron's hope that he may take heed.

BURHAN:v4p158/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p158/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p158/r3.claim: Arabic can phrase a certain outcome as doubtful for emphasis: warning that someone may regret an act conveys that regret is inevitable.
BURHAN:v4p158/r3.anchor: والعرب قد تخرج الكلام المتيقن في صورة المشكوك لاغراض فتقول

BURHAN:v4p158/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p158/r6.speaker: ابن الدهان
BURHAN:v4p158/r6.claim: Ibn al-Dahhan allows laʿalla to be used of an impossibility, citing a poem that hopes a bygone age might return.
BURHAN:v4p158/r6.anchor: ونص ابن الدهان في لعل جواز استعماله في المستحيل

BURHAN:v4p181/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p181/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p181/r2.claim: God's question about what people say is phrased from the addressees' perspective, as when Moses and Aaron are told to hope Pharaoh may heed them.
BURHAN:v4p181/r2.anchor: وقد علم الله أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى لكنه اراد لعله يفعل ذلك في رجائكما

BURHAN:v2p318/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.speaker: المحققون
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.claim: The learned explain divine exclamation, prayer, and hope from the hearer's perspective; Sibawayh reads 20:44 as Moses and Aaron acting on their own hope, which Ibn al-Da'i praises.
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.anchor: ثم قال المحققون التعجب مصروف إلى المخاطب ولهذا تلطف الزمخشري

BURHAN:v4p210/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p210/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p210/r2.claim: Another use of أو is equivalent to واو, including in the paired warning outcomes of 20:44.

BURHAN:v4p210/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p210/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p210/r5.claim: In 20:44, أو permits either of the two outcomes to be sought.

SULAMI:v1p445#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r1.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r1.claim: If God shows gentleness to one who claims divinity, how much more should He show gentleness to one who claims servanthood?
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r1.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : هذا رفقك بمن يدعي الربوبية فكيف رفقك بمن يدعي العبودية .

SULAMI:v1p445#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r2.claim: The gentleness shown to someone who harms you, to an enemy, and to enemies prompts asking how much greater it is toward those harmed for God, His friends, and His allies.
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r2.anchor: وقيل : هذا رفقك من أذاك ، فكيف رفقك بمن يؤذي فيك وهذا رفقك بمن عاداك ،

SULAMI:v1p445#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r3.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r3.claim: If God is gentle to one who denies and confronts Him, He is still more gentle to one who worships and submits.
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r3.anchor: وقال النهرجوري : هذا رفقك بمن جحدك وبارزك فكيف رفقك بمن عبدك وخضع لك .

SULAMI:v1p445#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r4.speaker: النهرجوري
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r4.claim: God told Moses He wished to repay Pharaoh's kindness to Moses at the start of his life, when Moses himself had not repaid it.
SULAMI:v1p445#4/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : قال الله لموسى : ﴿ فقولا له قولا لينا ﴾ . قال الله لموسى : إنه أحسن إليك في ابتداء أمرك

ITQAN:v2p479#3/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p479#3/r10.speaker: البرهان
ITQAN:v2p479#3/r10.claim: Al-Burhan says ʿasā and laʿalla from God are certain, though they express hope and doubt for humans; divine wording may reflect human uncertainty, as when Moses and Aaron are told to speak gently to Pharaoh.
ITQAN:v2p479#3/r10.anchor: وفي البرهان عسى ولعل من الله واجبتان وإن كانتا رجاء وطمعا في كلام المخلوقين لأن الخلق هم الذين يعرض لهم الشكوك والظنون والبارئ منزه عن ذلك

ITQAN:v2p504#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r1.claim: Laʿalla most commonly expresses expectation or hope for something welcome, and apprehension when the expected matter is unwelcome; al-Tanukhi says it can intensify the latter.
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r1.anchor: أشهرها التوقع وهو الترجي في المحبوب نحو ﴿ لعلكم تفلحون ﴾ والإشفاق في المكروه

ITQAN:v2p504#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r2.claim: In the command to speak gently to Pharaoh, laʿalla is causal: speak gently so that he may remember or fear.
ITQAN:v2p504#3/r2.anchor: الثاني التعليل وخرج عليه ﴿ فقولا له قولا لينا لعله يتذكر أو يخشى ﴾

ITQAN:v2p456/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p456/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p456/r8.claim: Aw may serve as a plain conjunction equivalent to wāw, joining both possible outcomes rather than setting up an exclusive choice.
ITQAN:v2p456/r8.anchor: ومطلق الجمع كالواو نحو ﴿ لعله يتذكر أو يخشى ﴾

ITQAN:v3p206/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p206/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p206/r1.claim: Expressions of divine amazement are redirected to the audience, since amazement as astonishment implies ignorance and God is exalted above it; the effect is to make people marvel.
ITQAN:v3p206/r1.anchor: إذا ورد التعجب من الله صرف إلى المخاطب

ITQAN:v3p206/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p206/r2.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v3p206/r2.claim: Sibawayh explains the divine language of hope as telling Moses and Aaron to go with their own hope and expectation that Pharaoh might remember or fear.
ITQAN:v3p206/r2.anchor: قال سيبويه في قوله تعالى ﴿ لعله يتذكر أو يخشى ﴾ المعنى اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما

TUSTARI:20:44/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:44/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TUSTARI:20:44/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses used to address Pharaoh as Abu Mus'ab and urge him to confess God's oneness and Moses' message.
TUSTARI:20:44/r1.anchor: حكي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أنه قال: كان موسى عليه السلام إذا دخل على فرعون

TUSTARI:20:44/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:44/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:44/r2.claim: God equipped Moses with patient restraint rather than rashness; the command to speak gently was not meant to predict Pharaoh's faith, but to teach Moses gracious speech that stirs hearts.
TUSTARI:20:44/r2.anchor: إن الله تعالى ألبس موسى عليه السلام لبسة المتأوبين، ونفى عنه عجلة المتهجمين

TUSTARI:20:44/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:44/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TUSTARI:20:44/r3.claim: The Prophet says hearts are disposed to love those who treat them well and hate those who mistreat them.
TUSTARI:20:44/r3.anchor: كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " جبلت القلوب على حب من أحسن إليها

TUSTARI:20:44/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:20:44/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:20:44/r4.claim: Gentle speech serves to establish Moses' proof and encourage the magicians and others whom God knows He will guide.
TUSTARI:20:44/r4.anchor: ليقطع به حجته، ويرغب من علم الله هدايته من السحرة وغيرهم

DAMGHANI:v1p55/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r3.claim: Aw can be additive, meaning 'and': Pharaoh may remember and fear; 80:3, 20:113, and 77:6 are grouped likewise.
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r3.anchor: أو بمعنى ألف صلة . قوله تعالى في سورة طه

DAMGHANI:v1p55/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r8.claim: The entry begins listing awwal as the first to disbelieve and the first to believe; its other examples fall outside this excerpt.
DAMGHANI:v1p55/r8.anchor: أول على أربعة أوجه أول من كفر . أول من آمن

DAMGHANI:v1p415/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p415/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p415/r9.claim: Laʿalla expresses hope here: Moses and Aaron hope Pharaoh may remember or fear.
DAMGHANI:v1p415/r9.anchor: لعل بمعنى الرجاء قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r1.claim: The particle aw can express doubt, as in seeing Zayd or ʿAmr, or choice, as when selecting a coin or its value in silver.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r1.anchor: ' أو ' : حرف يرد للشك . تقول : رأيت زيدا أو عمرا . ويرد للتخيير

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a poetic aw meaning bal, “rather”: the beloved is more pleasing to the eye.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r2.anchor: بدت مثل قرن الشمس في رونق الضحى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r3.speaker: جرير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r3.claim: Jarīr’s verse uses aw in the sense of waw, “and.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r3.anchor: نال الخلافة أو كانت له قدرا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r4.speaker: توبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r4.claim: Tawba’s line also uses aw as waw: her sin is upon her as well as her piety.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r7.claim: A second Quranic use is waw, “and,” including “perhaps he will remember and fear” and “do not obey a sinner or an ingrate.”
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن ' أو ' في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r1.claim: أو can express doubt, as in saying that one saw ʿAbd Allāh or Muḥammad.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r1.anchor: أو: تأتي للشك، تقول. رأيت عبد الله أو محمدا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r3.claim: Exegetes take أو as واو in examples such as عذرا أو نذرا, لعله يتذكر أو يخشى, and لعلهم يتقون أو يحدث لهم ذكرا.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p290#2/r3.anchor: هذا كله عند المفسرين بمعنى واو النسق

SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r1.speaker: أبو معاذ
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r1.claim: Abu Muʿadh reads قولا لينا with a lightened form, analogous to ميت beside ميت.
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو معاذ " قولا لينا " وهو تخفيف من لين كميت في ميت.

SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes لعل in its normal sense of hope, attributed to Moses and Aaron: they should go hoping Pharaoh will believe.
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r2.anchor: أحدها: أن " لعل " على بابها من الترجي: وذلك بالنسبة إلى المرسل، وهو موسى وهارون أي: اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما في إيمانه،

SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r3.claim: Sibawayh says every Qur'anic occurrence of لعل and عسى from God is certain or guaranteed, since ordinary hope cannot literally apply to God.
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r3.anchor: وعن سيبويه: " كل ما ورد في القرآن من لعل وعسى فهو من الله واجب " ،

SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r4.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ parses لعل causally as كي, 'so that,' as in working so that one may receive one's wages.
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r4.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء، قال: " كما تقول: اعمل لعلك تأخذ أجرك أي: كي تأخذ ".

SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r5.claim: The interrogative reading, 'will he remember or fear?', is untenable because divine questioning is as impossible as divine hope; preserving the ordinary sense is preferable to departing from it.
SAMIN-DURR:20:44/r5.anchor: والثالث: أنها استفهامية أي: هل يتذكر أو يخشى؟ وهذا قول ساقط؛

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r4.claim: Laʿalla denotes hope and expectation in ordinary language.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r4.anchor: لعل في اللغة ترج وطمع، تقول: لعلي أصير إلى خير

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r5.claim: Sībawayh explains the wording as Go, with your hope and expectation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r5.anchor: والمعنى عند سيبويه فيه: اذهبا على رجائكما

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r6.claim: Although God knew Pharaoh would not remember or fear, the messengers had to make the proof clear; the obligation follows from clarification and evidence.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r6.anchor: وقد علم الله عز وجل أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r7.claim: Messengers do not know the unseen or whether people will accept them; their real hope is part of how they are sent, and God's knowledge is not human knowledge that establishes proof.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r7.anchor: وإنما تبعث الرسل وهي لا تعلم الغيب ولا تدري أيقبل منها

ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r8.claim: The hope expressed here is the pattern on which all messengers are sent.
ZAJJAJ:v3p357/r8.anchor: فمعنى: (لعله يتذكر أو يخشى). هو الذي عليه بعث

ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r1.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r1.claim: Razi reads the tentative clause as the messenger's intention or hope of prompting Pharaoh, not uncertainty in God's knowledge of his future response.
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r1.anchor: it relates to the intention or hope with which the message-bearer should approach his task (Razi).

ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r2.claim: Because Qur'anic narratives convey enduring truths about human behavior, Asad says the command to speak gently remains valid for all times and every effort at conversion.
ASAD-NOTES:20:42#n28/r2.anchor: to speak to one particular sinner "in a mild manner, so that he might (have a chance to] bethink himself" retains its validity

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.claim: Ta-Ha presents a joint mission: both are sent, answer in fear, receive reassurance, deliver the message, and are addressed by Pharaoh together, making Aaron Moses's partner in conveying the message.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8#2/r2.anchor: فقد أمر كلاً من موسى وهرون بالذهاب بآياته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r1.speaker: أبو معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r1.claim: Abu Muadh reads لينا with a light nūn rather than doubling it.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r2.claim: The ف links gentle speech to Pharaoh's transgression: softness can break stubbornness and soften tyrants' hardened hearts; the order is not merely parental care.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r2.anchor: والفاء لترتيب ما بعدها على طغيانه فان تليين القول مما يكسر سورة عناد العتاة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r3.claim: Remembering means reflecting, then being fair to oneself and yielding to truth, which can lead to faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r3.anchor: ويتامل فيبذل النصفة من نفسه والاذعان للحق فيدعوه ذلك إلى الأيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the instruction as avoiding harshness and speaking gently when inviting Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r4.anchor: كما قال ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما : لاتعنفاه فى قولكماوارفقا به فى الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r5.claim: Examples of gentle invitation are the offer in 20:47 and Moses' courteous question in al-Naziʿat, which presents purification and guidance as an invitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r5.anchor: ومنها ما فى النازعات وهو ( هل لك إلى أن تزكى واهديك إلى ربك فتخشى )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس وسفيان الثوري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r6.claim: A view, attributed to Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Sufyan al-Thawri, says they should address Pharaoh by a kunya, implying it is permissible to use a kunya for an unbeliever; Pharaoh had four kunyas.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r6.anchor: وقيل : كنياه واستدل به على جواز تكنية الكافر وروى ذلك عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r7.claim: Another view says they should promise Pharaoh lasting youth, a kingdom he keeps until death, and continuing pleasures of food, drink, and sex.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : عداه شبابا لايهرم بعده وملكا لاينزع منه إلا بالموت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r8.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r8.claim: Al-Hasan's proposed gentle message reminds Pharaoh that he has a Lord and an afterlife, and invites belief for entry to Paradise and safety from Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r8.anchor: وعن الحسن قولا له : أن لك ربا وان لك معادا وان بين يديك جنة ونارا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r9.claim: Some say the promise should precede the threat, supported by a maxim that promises soften ignorant tribes; no poet is named.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r9.anchor: وقيل : أمرهما سبحانه بأن يقدما له الوعد على الوعيد من غير تعيين قول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r10.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r10.claim: Ikrima identifies the gentle word as لا إله إلا الله, gentle because it is easy on the tongue; al-Alusi calls this the most remote view and favors Ibn Abbas's explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r10.anchor: وروى عن عكرمة أن القول اللين لا إلة إلا الله ولينه خفته على اللسان

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r11.speaker: الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشى
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r11.claim: Al-Fadl ibn ʿIsa al-Raqashi would reflect in recitation that God seeks the affection of one who opposes Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r11.anchor: وكان الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشى إذا تلا هذه الآية قال : يا من يتحبب إلى من يعاديه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r12.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r12.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh wept and marveled at God's gentleness toward someone claiming to be a god, asking how God treats one who confesses Him as God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r12.anchor: وقرأت عند يحيى بن معاذ فبكى وقال : إلهى هذا رفقك بمن يقول انا الاله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r13.claim: The verse supports the recommendation to speak gently when admonishing even a wicked person.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#3/r13.anchor: وفيها دليل على استحباب الانة القول للظالك عند وعظه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r1.claim: Fear means considering that Moses and Aaron may be right and that denial could bring destruction, which also prompts faith; remembering is placed first as the response of the grounded.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r1.anchor: أن يكون الأمر كما تصفان فيجره انكاره إلى الهلكة وذلك يدعوه إلى الأيمان أيضا إلا أن الأول للراسخين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r2.claim: One report says Pharaoh remembered when the Nile receded; he prostrated in supplication, then saw the water follow his horse's hoof, learning God's immense forbearance and kindness.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r2.anchor: وقيل : يتذكر حاله حين احتبس النيل فسار إلى شاطئه وابعد وخر لله تعالى ساجدا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r3.claim: Another explanation takes fearing as Pharaoh's becoming wary of God's power and punishment; al-Alusi says the preceding explanation is the one to rely on.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r3.anchor: أو يخشى ويحذر من بطش الله تعالى وعذابه سبحانه والمعول على ما تقدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r4.claim: Here لعل expresses hope addressed to Moses and Aaron; the clause is circumstantial to their implied subject in قولا, and أو prevents excluding either outcome.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r4.anchor: ولعل للترجى وهو راجع للمخاطبين والجملة في محل النصب حال من ضميرها في ( قولا )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r5.claim: They should undertake the mission with genuine expectation that their efforts will bear fruit, exerting themselves fully rather than acting halfheartedly.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r5.anchor: باشرا الأمر مباشرة من يرجو ويطمع أن يثمر عمله ولا يخيب سعيه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r6.claim: An alternative makes the circumstantial clause refer to the dual subject of اذهبا; al-Alusi prefers its attachment to قولا.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r6.anchor: وقيل : حال من ضميرهما ( اذهبا ) والأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim, reportedly takes لعل as an interrogative: whether Pharaoh might remember or fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r7.anchor: وقيل : لعل هنا للاستفهام أي هل يتذكر أو يخشى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r8.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r8.claim: Al-Farra takes لعل causally, meaning so that; al-Alusi notes this sense is also held by al-Akhfash, al-Kisaʾi, and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r8.anchor: وقال الفراء : هي هنا بمعنى كى التعليلية وهى أحد معانيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r9.speaker: الواقدي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r9.claim: Al-Baghawi transmits from al-Waqidi that every Quranic لعل is causal except لعلكم تخلدون, which means as if you would live forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r9.anchor: بل حكى البغوى عن الواقدى أن جميع ما في القرآن من لعل فانها للتعليل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r10.speaker: أبو مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r10.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits through al-Suddi from Abu Malik that لعل generally means so that in the Quran, except in the Shuʿara verse where it means as if you would live forever.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبى حاتم من طريق السدى عن أبى مالك قال :

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r11.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r11.claim: Al-Alusi also cites Qatada as saying that the verse was read in this way, in the discussion of the exception concerning لعلكم تخلدون.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r11.anchor: وأخرج عن قتادة أنه قال : قرئ كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r12.claim: Al-Alusi calls the similitude reading of لعل unusual and unattested by grammarians, and considers the interrogative reading here unlikely.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r12.anchor: ولا يخفى أن كونها للتشبيه غريب لم يذكره النحاة وحملها على الأستفهام هنا بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r13.claim: Although a causal reading may first suggest itself, al-Alusi follows al-Bahr: the correct and familiar sense is hope, figuratively used for general request by some theologians.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r13.anchor: لكن الصحيح كما في البحر أنها للترجى وهو المشهور من معانيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r14.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r14.claim: The Imam says only God knows why the messengers were sent to Pharaoh despite knowing he would not believe; one should submit rather than object, a stance al-Alusi endorses.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p195/r14.anchor: وزعم الأمام أنه لا يعلم سر الارسال اليه مع علمه تعالى بامتناع حصول الأيمان منه إلا الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r1.speaker: بعض المتبعين لمن قال بنجاة فرعون
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r1.claim: Some advocates of Pharaoh's salvation argue that God's لعل must come true, so one of remembering or fearing occurred and secured salvation; al-Alusi says his earlier analysis refutes this inference.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r1.anchor: واستدل بعض المتبعين لمن قال بنجاة فرعون بهذه الآية فقال : أن لعل كذا من الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r2.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that Pharaoh remembered and feared only at drowning and that this satisfies the verse; the clause cannot include the alleged last-moment response.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p196/r2.anchor: ولا حاجة بنا إلى ما قيل من أنه تذكر وخشى لكن حيث لم ينفعه ذلك وهو حين الغرق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r9.claim: Moses and Aaron are told to deal tactfully and gently with Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r9.anchor: {فقولا له قولا لينا} يقول: دارياه وارفقا معه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says they should not speak harshly to Pharaoh.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لا تعنفا في قولكما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r11.speaker: السدي وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r11.claim: Al-Suddi and Ikrima say gentle speech meant addressing Pharaoh by his kunya, Abu al-Abbas or Abu al-Walid.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r11.anchor: وقال السدي وعكرمة: كنياه فقولا يا أبا العباس، وقيل: يا أبا الوليد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r12.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r12.claim: Muqatil identifies gentle speech with the invitation to purify himself and be guided to his Lord and fear Him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r12.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعني القول اللين: "هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r13.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r13.claim: Another explanation says gentle speech was commanded because Pharaoh had a right of upbringing.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r13.anchor: وقيل: أمر باللطافة في القول لما له من حق التربية.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r14.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r14.claim: Al-Suddi recounts Moses offering Pharaoh lasting youth and kingship until death, worldly pleasures, and Paradise if he accepted faith; Pharaoh was tempted but Haman mocked the idea of a deity becoming a subject, turning him from it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p274/r14.anchor: وقال السدي: القول اللين: أن موسى أتاه ووعده على قبول الإيمان شبابا لا يهرم، وملكا لا ينزع منه إلا بالموت،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r1.claim: Aaron was in Egypt; God ordered Moses to go to him and inspired Aaron to meet Moses, whom he met after a day's journey and then told what had been revealed to him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r1.anchor: وكان هارون يومئذ بمصر، فأمر الله موسى أن يأتي هارون وأوحى إلى هارون وهو بمصر أن يتلقى موسى، فتلقاه إلى مرحلة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r2.claim: The hope is that Pharaoh will take heed, fear, and submit to Islam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r2.anchor: {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} أي: يتعظ ويخاف فيسلم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r3.claim: Although God already knew Pharaoh would not believe, the command means the two messengers should go with hope and expectation while God's decree remains beyond their charge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r3.anchor: فإن قيل: كيف قال: {لعله يتذكر} وقد سبق علمه أنه لا يتذكر ولا يسلم؟. قيل: معناه اذهبا على رجاء منكما وطمع، وقضاء الله وراء أمركما.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r4.speaker: الحسين بن الفضل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r4.claim: Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl says the phrase refers to someone besides Pharaoh: a witness may reflect and fear on seeing God's kindness to a creature who claimed divinity.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r4.anchor: وقال الحسين بن الفضل: هو ينصرف إلى غير فرعون، مجازه: لعله يتذكر متذكر، ويخشى خاش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r5.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن عمر الوراق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r5.claim: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Warraq says God's laʿalla is certain; Pharaoh did remember and fear while drowning, when it could no longer benefit him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r5.anchor: وقال أبو بكر محمد بن عمر الوراق: "لعل " من الله واجب (3) ولقد تذكر فرعون وخشي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r6.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh wept on hearing the verse and prayed: if God is gentle with one who says “I am god,” how gentle is He with one who says “You are God?”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p275/r6.anchor: وقرأ رجل عند يحيى بن معاذ هذه الآية: {فقولا له قولا لينا} فبكى يحيى، وقال: إلهي هذا رفقك

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r1.claim: Gentle speech resembles an invitation framed as an offer and counsel; this avoids provoking Pharaoh's violence or may show respect for his having raised Moses.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r1.anchor: فإنه دعوة في صورة عرض ومشورة حذرا أن تحمله الحماقة

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r2.claim: It is said they addressed Pharaoh by one of his three kunyas: Abu al-Abbas, Abu al-Walid, or Abu Murra.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r2.anchor: وقيل كنياه وكان له ثلاث كنى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r3.claim: Another report says they promised him everlasting youth and a kingdom that would last until his death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r3.anchor: وقيل عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده وملكا لا يزول

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r4.claim: The hope clause may modify ذهبا or قولا, telling them to act in hope their effort will bear fruit; the hopeful exerts himself, unlike the despairing person who only pretends to act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r4.anchor: متعلق ب { اذهبا } أو «قولا» أي: باشرا الأمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r5.claim: The mission establishes proof, removes excuses, and displays signs; remembrance is hoped for if truth is recognized, while fear may still arise if it is suspected, hence the order of the verbs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:44/r5.anchor: الفائدة في إرسالهما والمبالغة عليهما في الاجتهاد مع علمه بأنه لا يؤمن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r3.claim: Those who command right should begin with the gentlest approach; gentle speech leaves Pharaoh no excuse or grounds for complaint.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r3.anchor: بما ينبغي لكل آمر بالمعروف من الأخذ بالأحسن فالأحسن والأسهل فالأسهلن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r4.claim: Gentle speech may prompt Pharaoh to recall God’s care through his changing stages and recognize God as his Lord, turning from error to faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r4.anchor: ما مر له من تطوير الله له في أطوار مختلفة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r5.claim: Alternatively, Pharaoh may fear the consequences of their message, suspect it is true, and send the Children of Israel with Moses and Aaron.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r5.anchor: أو يصل غلى حال من يخاف عاقبة قولكما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r6.claim: The expression of hope describes a state reasonably hoped for by the speakers; the Qur’an follows human expectations in dialogue, while God knows what will occur.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r6.anchor: ومعنى الترجي أن يكون حاله حال من يرجى منه ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r7.speaker: سيبويه
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r7.claim: Biqāʿī cites Sibawayh’s discussion of verbal nouns and names for the grammatical account of this expression of hope.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r7.anchor: قاله سيبويه في باب من النكرة يجري مجرى ما فيه الألف واللام من المصادر والأسماء

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r1.speaker: الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشي
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r1.claim: Al-Faḍl ibn ʿĪsā al-Raqāshī turns the instruction into an exhortation: if God shows affection to an enemy, how much more to one who serves and calls upon Him.
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r1.anchor: عن الفضل بن عيسى الرقاشي أنه تلا هذه الآية {فقولا له قولا لينا} فقال: يا من يتحبب إلى من يعاديه فكيف بمن يتولى ويناديه

DURR-FULL:v5p580/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “perhaps he will remember” as “will he remember?”
DURR-FULL:v5p580/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {لعله يتذكر} قال: هل يتذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r5.claim: Gentle speech invites and persuades compliance while treating the listener as capable of sound judgment and of distinguishing truth, without insulting or belittling him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r5.anchor: والقول اللين : الكلام الدال على معاني الترغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r1.claim: Calling words gentle extends physical softness to speech carrying fine meanings; physical softness is moist, pliable touch, and the poet Amr ibn Kulthum uses تلينا for yielding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r1.anchor: فشبه الكلام المشتمل على المعاني الحسنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r2.claim: Gentleness marks truthful preaching, illustrated by 16:125, 3:159, and Moses' invitation in 79:18–19 and greeting in 20:47; the goal is guidance, not harsh display.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r2.anchor: واللين من شعار الدعوة إلى الحق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r3.claim: If gentleness fails with an arrogant rejecter, harsher admonition is allowed, as the exception for wrongdoers and Moses' warning demonstrate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r3.anchor: فإذا لم ينفع اللين مع المدعو وأعرض واستكبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r4.claim: لعل either figuratively depicts God's invitation as hopeful, or instructs Moses and Pharaoh to hope; in the second reading it elicits the hearer's hope rather than reporting God's actual hope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r4.anchor: والترجي المستفاد من ( لعل ) إما تمثيل لشأن الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r5.claim: تذكر here means reflective consideration: Pharaoh might recognize the truth or fear punishment and comply cautiously; recognition corrects his belief that he is right, while fear reflects uncertainty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p225/r5.anchor: والتذكر : من الذكر بضم الذال أي النظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r6.claim: One group explains gentle speech as addressing Pharaoh by his kunya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r6.anchor: والقول اللين قالت فرقة: معناه كنياه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r7.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r7.claim: Another group says Moses and Aaron were instructed to make their wording courteous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة بل أمرهما بتحسين الكلمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the second view: convey the intended meaning fully, then phrase it gently, since gentle address better achieves the aim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r8.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا هو الوجه، وذلك أن كل من يريد دعاء إنسان إلى أمر يكرهه فإنما الوجه أن يحرر في عبارته بالمعنى الذي يريد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r9.claim: God instructed Moses and Aaron to make a complete invitation to Pharaoh using gentle speech.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r9.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى موسى وهارون أن يسلكا مع فرعون إكمال الدعوة في لين من القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r10.claim: The expectation in لعله belongs to the two human messengers' hope and anticipation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p45#2/r10.anchor: وقوله لعله معناه على رجائكما وطمعكما فالتوقع فيها إنما هو راجع إلى جهة البشر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني وعاصم الجحدري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r1.claim: Abu ʿImran al-Jawni and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read layyinan with a quiescent yāʾ; it means gently and kindly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمران الجوني وعاصم الجحدري لينا باسكان الياء أي لطفيا رفيقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r2.speaker: خالد بن معدان عن معاذ والضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r2.claim: One view is to say: “There is no god but God alone, without partner,” transmitted from Muʿadh and Ibn ʿAbbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r2.anchor: أحدها قولا له قل لا اله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له رواه خالد ابن معدان عن معاذ والضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r3.claim: Another view identifies the gentle words as the invitation “Will you purify yourself and let me guide you to your Lord, so you may fear Him?”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r3.anchor: والثاني انه قوله ﴿ هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى ﴾ النازعات 1819 قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r4.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r4.claim: A third view says Moses addressed Pharaoh by a kunya; ʿIkrima transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbas, and al-Suddi also holds it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r4.anchor: والثالث كنياه رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس وبه قال السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r5.claim: One reported kunya for Pharaoh is Abu Murra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r5.anchor: أحدها أبو مرة رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r6.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r6.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi gives Pharaoh's kunya as Abu Musʿab.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r6.anchor: والثاني أبو مصعب ذكره أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r7.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r7.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits two further proposed kunyās for Pharaoh: Abu al-ʿAbbas and Abu al-Walid.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r7.anchor: والثالث أبو العباس والرابع أبو الوليد حكاهما الثعلبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the gentle words tell Pharaoh that he has a Lord and a return, with Paradise and Fire ahead.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r8.anchor: والقول الرابع قولا له إن لك ربا وإن لك معادا وإن بين يديك جنة ونارا قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r9.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi recounts Moses offering Pharaoh continuing youth and kingship until death, then Paradise; Haman later turned Pharaoh against the offer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r9.anchor: والخامس أن القول اللين أن موسى أتاه فقال له تؤمن بما جئت به وتعبد رب العالمين على أن لك شبابك فلا تهرم وتكون ملكا لا ينزع منك حتى تموت فاذا مت دخلت الجنة فأعجبه ذلك فلما جاء هامان أخبره بما قال موسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r10.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r10.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh reflects that if God treated gently one who claimed divinity, His gentleness toward one who affirms God must be greater.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r10.anchor: وحكي عن يحيى بن معاذ أنه قرأ هذه الآية فقال إلهي هذا رفقك بمن يقول أنا إله فكيف رفقك بمن يقول أنت إله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r11.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj says laʿalla expresses hope or expectation in Arabic; God addresses people in terms they understand.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r11.anchor: قال الزجاج لعل في اللغة ترج وطمع تقول لعلي أصير إلى خير فخاطب الله عز وجل العباد بما يعقلون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r12.speaker: سيبويه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r12.claim: Sibawayh paraphrases the command as “go with your hope and expectation”; God already knows Pharaoh will not remember or fear, but the messengers do not know the unseen and must deliver proof while hoping it is accepted.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r12.anchor: والمعنى عند سيبويه اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما والعلم من الله تعالى من وراء ما يكون وقدعلم أنه لا يتذكر ولا يخشى إلا أن الحجة إنما تجب عليه بالآية والبرهان وإنما تبعث الرسل وهي لا تعلم الغيب ولا تدري ايقبل منها أم لا وهم يرجون ويطمعون أن يقبل منهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r13.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r13.claim: Al-Farraʾ takes laʿalla here to mean “so that he may remember.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري ومذهب الفراء في هذا كي يتذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r14.speaker: خالد بن معدان عن معاذ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r14.claim: Khalid ibn Maʿdan transmits from Muʿadh that Pharaoh did remember and fear when drowning, before leaving this world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r14.anchor: وروى خالد بن معدان عن معاذ قال والله ما كان فرعون ليخرج من الدنيا حتى يتذكر أو يخشى لهذه الآية وإنه تذكر وخشي لما أدركه الغرق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r15.speaker: كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r15.claim: Kaʿb swears that the Torah says God told Moses to speak gently and that He would harden Pharaoh's heart so he would not believe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287#2/r15.anchor: وقال كعب والذي يحلف به كعب إنه لمكتوب في التوراة فقولا له قولا لينا وسأقسي قلبه فلا يؤمن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r6.claim: The verse is a profound lesson: although Pharaoh was supremely arrogant and Moses God's chosen servant, Moses and Aaron were commanded to address him gently.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r6.anchor: هذه الآية فيها عبرة عظيمة، وهو أن فرعون في غاية العتو والاستكبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r7.speaker: يزيد الرقاشي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r7.claim: Yazid al-Raqqashi remarks that God endears Himself to one who opposes Him, so how much more to one who accepts and calls upon Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r7.anchor: كما قال يزيد الرقاشي عند قوله: {فقولا له قولا لينا} : يا من يتحبب إلى من يعاديه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r8.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r8.claim: Wahb says the gentle words tell Pharaoh that God is nearer to pardon and forgiveness than to anger and punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r8.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه: قولا له: إني إلى العفو والمغفرة أقرب مني إلى الغضب والعقوبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r9.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r9.claim: Ikrima identifies the gentle utterance as the testimony that there is no god but God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة في قوله: {فقولا له قولا لينا} قال: لا إله إلا الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r10.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد عن الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r10.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd reports Hasan al-Basri's view: excuse Pharaoh by telling him he has a Lord and a return, with Paradise and Hell ahead.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r10.anchor: عمرو بن عبيد، عن الحسن البصري: {فقولا له قولا لينا} أعذرا إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r11.speaker: علي عن الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r11.claim: Ali's transmitted gloss is “كنه”; Sufyan al-Thawri likewise reportedly glossed it “كنه بأبي مرة.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r11.anchor: وقال بقية، عن علي بن هارون، عن رجل، عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، عن النزال بن سبرة، عن علي في قوله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r12.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r12.claim: Ibn Kathir concludes that their invitation should use soft, gentle, accessible words, which better reach hearts and prove more effective; he connects this to the command to invite with wisdom and good counsel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r12.anchor: والحاصل من أقوالهم أن دعوتهما له تكون بكلام رقيق لين قريب سهل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r1.claim: Remembrance means turning back from what is forbidden, while fear means attaining obedience; the wording echoes the description of one who seeks to remember or fear God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r1.anchor: فالتذكر: الرجوع عن المحذور، والخشية: تحصيل الطاعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r2.claim: Hasan says Moses and Aaron should not demand Pharaoh's destruction before they have first given him an excuse and warning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري [في قوله] (3) {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r3.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، ويروى لأمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a poem attributed to Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, also attributed to Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt by Ibn Ishaq, depicting Moses and Aaron calling Pharaoh to God and asking who made the heavens, light, sun, and vegetation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p295/r3.anchor: وهاهنا نذكر شعر زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل، ويروى لأمية بن أبي الصلت فيما ذكره ابن إسحاق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r7.claim: A reading lightens layyinan to līnan, “gentle speech.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r8.claim: The gentle invitation resembles the question and counsel, “Will you purify yourself? Shall I guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him?”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r8.anchor: نحو قوله تعالى : { هل لك إلى أن تزكى * وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r9.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r9.claim: One view says they were to promise Pharaoh lasting youth, kingship until death, and continued pleasures of food, drink, and sex until he died.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r9.anchor: وقيل : عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده ، وملكا لا ينزع منه إلا بالموت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r10.claim: Another view says they should avoid affronting Pharaoh and speak gently because he had raised Moses and had something like a father’s claim.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r10.anchor: وقيل : لا تجبهاه بما يكره ، وألطفا له في القول ، لما له من حق تربية موسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r11.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r11.claim: Another view says they should address Pharaoh by a kunya; he had three: Abū al-ʿAbbās, Abū al-Walīd, and Abū Murra.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : كنياه وهو من ذوي الكنى الثلاث : أبو العباس ، وأبو الوليد ، وأبو مرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r12.claim: The hopeful wording instructs them to act expecting their effort may bear fruit, striving with all their strength rather than despairing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r12.anchor: والترجي لهما ، أي : اذهبا على رجائكما وطمعكما ، وباشرا الأمر مباشرة من يرجو ويطمع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r13.claim: Sending messengers despite knowing Pharaoh would not believe establishes proof and removes his excuse, as the counterfactual at 20:134 shows.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r13.anchor: وجدوى إرسالهما إليه مع العلم بأنه لن يؤمن إلزام الحجة وقطع المعذرة { ولو أنا أهلكناهم بعذاب من قبله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r14.claim: To remember here is to reflect, consider, and then give oneself fairly to the truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r14.anchor: أي : يتذكر ويتأمل فيبذل النصفة من نفسه والإذعان للحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r15.claim: He may fear that Moses and Aaron’s warning is true and that denial will lead him to ruin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p66#2/r15.anchor: أن يكون الأمر كما تصفان ، فيجره إنكاره إلى الهلكة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r9.claim: One explanation is that the brothers should address Pharaoh gently and softly.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r10.claim: Al-Suddi says they were to address Pharaoh by his kunya.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r10.anchor: كنياه , قاله السدي وقيل إن كنية فرعون

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r11.claim: The reported kunyas of Pharaoh are Abu Murra and Abu al-Walid.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r11.anchor: كنية فرعون أبو مرة , وقيل أبو الوليد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r12.claim: A further possibility is to begin with enticement before warning, softening Pharaoh before confronting him with threat.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r12.anchor: أن يبدأه بالرغبة قبل الرهبة , ليلين بها فيتوطأ بعدها من رهبة ووعيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r13.speaker: بعض المتصوفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r13.claim: Some Sufis marvel that God treats an enemy with such gentleness and ask how gentle He must be to one who supports Him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r13.anchor: يا رب هذا رفقك لمن عاداك , فكيف رفقك بمن والاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r14.claim: It is said Pharaoh had treated Moses well while raising him, so gentleness repaid that kindness when Moses could not repay him otherwise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p404#2/r14.anchor: وقيل إن فرعون كان يحسن لموسى حين رباه , فأراد أن يجعل رفقه به مكافأة له

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r6.claim: Gentle speech means addressing Pharaoh respectfully by his kunya and inviting him to purify himself and follow his Lord so he may fear God.
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r6.anchor: يقول: ادعواه الكنية، يعنى بالقول اللين

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r7.claim: The gentle invitation gives Pharaoh the opportunity to remember or fear God.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r1.claim: Speak gently perhaps because Pharaoh raised Moses; another possibility is addressing him by a kunya or flattering him with lasting youth and kingship.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r1.anchor: الطفا له في القول لما له من حق تربية موسى أو كياه وهو من ذوي الكي الثلاث أبو العباس وأبو الوليد وأبو مرة أو عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده وملكا لا ينزع عنه إلا بالموت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r2.claim: A model is “Will you purify yourself and let me guide you to your Lord, so that you fear Him?”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r2.anchor: أو هو قوله هل لك إلى أن تزكى وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى فظاهره الاستفهام والمشورة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r3.claim: He may take heed, reflect, and yield to truth.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r4.claim: He may fear the message is true and denial brings ruin; “perhaps” expresses the brothers' hope though God knows Pharaoh will not believe, and the mission establishes proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r4.anchor: أي يخاف أن يكون الأمر كما تصفان فيجره انكاره على الهلكة وإنما قال لعله يتذكر مع علمه أنه لا يتذكر لان الترجي لهما

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r5.claim: Another view reads “perhaps a reminder will remember or a fearful person will fear”; many did.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r5.anchor: وقيل معناه لعله يتذكر متذكر أو يخشى خاش وقد كان ذلك من كثير من الناس

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r6.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r6.claim: Another view says laʿalla from God is certain: Pharaoh remembered and feared, but too late for repentance to benefit him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r6.anchor: وقيل لعل من الله تعالى واجب وقد تذكر ولكن حين لم ينفعه التذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r7.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r7.claim: A report says Pharaoh remembered, feared, and wanted to follow Moses, but Hāmān stopped him; Pharaoh decided nothing without Hāmān.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r7.anchor: وقيل تذكر فرعون وخشي وأراد اتباع موسى فمنعه هامان وكان لا يقطع امرا دونه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r8.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r8.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh wept at God's gentleness toward one claiming to be a god and asked how gentle God is to one who calls Him God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p56/r8.anchor: وتليت عند يحيى بن معاذ فبكى وقال هذا رفقك بمن يقول أنا إله فكيف بمن قال أنت الإله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r4.claim: The verse supports enjoining right and forbidding wrong gently, especially toward the powerful, when God grants protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r4.anchor: الثانية: في قوله تعالى: { فقولا له قولا لينا } دليل على جواز الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر، وأن ذلك يكون باللين من القول

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r5.speaker: الكلبي وعكرمة وابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r5.claim: Al-Kalbī, ʿIkrima, Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and al-Suddī say gentle speech means using Pharaoh's kunya.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r5.anchor: فقالت فرقة منهم الكلبي وعكرمة: معناه كنياه وقاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والسدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r6.claim: One proposed kunya for Pharaoh is Abū al-ʿAbbās.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r7.claim: Another proposed kunya for Pharaoh is Abū al-Walīd.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
