QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r8.claim: A third proposed kunya for Pharaoh is Abū Murra.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r8.anchor: وقيل: أبو مرة فعلى هذا القول تكنية الكافر جائزة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r9.claim: Under the kunya interpretation, it is permissible to address a prominent unbeliever respectfully, especially in hope of his conversion; Qurṭubī says hope is not a necessary condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r9.anchor: فعلى هذا القول تكنية الكافر جائزة إذا كان وجيها ذا شرف وطمع بإسلامه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r10.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r10.claim: The Prophet said to honor a people's notable when he comes; Qurṭubī counts using a kunya as honor.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r10.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إذا أتاكم كريم قوم فأكرموه " ولم يقل وإن طمعتم في إسلامه

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r11.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r11.claim: The Prophet called Ṣafwān ibn Umayya Abū Wahb.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r11.anchor: وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لصفوان بن أمية: " انزل أبا وهب " فكناه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r12.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r12.claim: The Prophet referred to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy as Abū Ḥubāb when speaking to Saʿd.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r12.anchor: وقال لسعد: " ألم تسمع ما يقوله أبو حباب " يعني عبد الله بن أبي.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r14.claim: Another proposed appeal promised lasting youth, a kingdom kept until death, four hundred extra years, and Paradise if Pharaoh believed and worshipped the Lord of the worlds.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r14.anchor: وقيل قال له موسى: تؤمن بما جئت به، وتعبد رب العالمين على أن لك شبابا لا يهرم إلى الموت،

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies gentle speech with Moses' invitation to purify oneself and be guided to one's Lord so as to fear Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r1.anchor: فقل هل لك إلى أن تزكى * وأهديك إلى ربك فتخشى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r2.claim: Another view identifies it as Moses saying he and Aaron were messengers of Pharaoh's Lord, using a title dearer to Pharaoh than other words.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r2.anchor: وقد قيل إن القول اللين قول موسى: يا فرعون إنا رسولا ربك رب العالمين.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r3.claim: Qurṭubī defines gentle speech as speech without harshness and says others should follow the prophets' model in admonition.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r3.anchor: قلت: القول اللين هو القول الذي لا خشونة فيه يقال: لان الشيء يلين لينا وشيء لين

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r4.claim: The instruction accords with the command to speak beautifully to people.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه وغيره من كبراء النحويين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r5.claim: Sībawayh and other leading grammarians say laʿalla expresses human hope or expectation, not uncertainty in God.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r5.anchor: فالتوقع فيها إنما هو راجع إلى جهة البشر قاله كبراء النحويين: سيبويه وغيره

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj calls laʿalla a term of hope and expectation used to address people in terms they understand.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: «لعل» لفظة طمع وترج فخاطبهم بما يعقلون.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r7.claim: Some construe laʿalla as a question: see whether Pharaoh will remember.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: «لعل» هاهنا بمعنى الاستفهام، والمعنى فانظر هل يتذكر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r8.claim: Another grammatical explanation gives laʿalla the sense كي, so that.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r9.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says God is reporting Hārūn's words to Moses: perhaps Pharaoh will remember or fear.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو إخبار من الله تعالى عن قول هارون لموسى لعله يتذكر أو يخشى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r10.claim: Abū Bakr al-Warrāq and others say laʿalla and ʿasā throughout the Qurʾān refer to what has occurred: Pharaoh remembered and feared at drowning, but it did not help him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن لعل وعسى في جميع القرآن لما قد وقع. وقد تذكر فرعون حين أدركه الغرق وخشي

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r11.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r11.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh marvels that God was gentle toward someone claiming to be god, then asks how gentle He is toward one who acknowledges Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r11.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ في هذه الآية هذا رفقك بمن يقول أنا الإله فكيف رفقك بمن يقول أنت الإله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r12.claim: A report says Pharaoh leaned toward Moses' invitation; his wife believed and urged faith, while Hāmān warned he would lose mastery, promised to restore youth, and dyed his beard black, becoming the first to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r12.anchor: فشاور هامان فقال: لا تفعل بعد أن كنت مالكا تصير مملوكا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r13.claim: Pharaoh professed faith and feared at drowning, but this did not benefit him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44#2/r13.anchor: وقد تذكر فرعون حين أدركه الغرق وخشي فقال:

BURSEVI:v5p298/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p298/r1.claim: The mission's benefit returned to Moses and Aaron, not Pharaoh: their messengership and warning would be established, while Pharaoh's denial would make his disbelief manifest, as in the cited verse.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r1.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" اعلم أن فائدة إتيانهما ورسالتهما إلى فرعون

BURSEVI:v5p298/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r2.claim: They should address Pharaoh gently and kindly, without roughness or scolding; gentleness adorns whatever enters it, while harshness mars it.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r2.anchor: كلماه باللين والرفق من غير خشونة ولا تعنيف ويسرا ولا تعسرا

BURSEVI:v5p298/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r3.claim: Moses was sharp and hard-tempered, becoming so angry that his cap seemed to catch fire; gentleness was prescribed to soften his temper and make him forbearing.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r3.anchor: وكان في موسى حدة وصلابة وخشونة بحيث إذا غضب اشتعلت قلنسوته نارا

BURSEVI:v5p298/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r4.claim: One view contrasts Muhammad's gentle and merciful temperament, which suited the command to severity, with Moses' hard and forceful temperament, which suited the command to gentleness; each completes a different divine quality.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r4.anchor: طبع الحبيب كان على اللين والرحمة فلذا أمر بالغلظة كما قال تعالى : {واغلظ عليهم}

BURSEVI:v5p298/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r5.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v5p298/r5.claim: The prophetic maxim “Adopt God's qualities” supports embodying both majesty and beauty in the manner suited to each prophet's station.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r5.anchor: وقد قال عليه السلام : "تخلقوا بأخلاق الله"

BURSEVI:v5p298/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r6.claim: Pharaoh was a tyrannical king who would grow more defiant under harsh admonition; gentleness was safer and more effective, while sternness can suit the common people.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r6.anchor: وأيضا إن فرعون كان من الملوك الجبابرة ومن عادتهم

BURSEVI:v5p298/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r7.claim: Harsh words might have provoked Pharaoh to strike or kill Moses, so gentleness also protected Moses.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r7.anchor: فلو كان في قول موسى خشونة لم يحتمل طبع فرعون بل هاج غضبه فلعله يقصد موسى بضرب أو قتل

BURSEVI:v5p298/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r8.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v5p298/r8.claim: At the beginning of a mission, the preacher should give the addressee room to consider the message; only after defiance and obstinacy do harshness and severity become appropriate.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r8.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" إنما أمرهما بذلك لأنه كان ابتداء حال الدعوة

BURSEVI:v5p298/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298/r9.claim: Gentleness and sternness can each be praised or blamed depending on circumstances; sound judgment follows what the situation requires and avoids either extreme.
BURSEVI:v5p298/r9.anchor: فكل من اللين والخشونة يمدح به طورا ويذم به طورا بحسب اختلاف الواقع

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r1.claim: A Persian couplet commends joining gentleness with firmness and likens striking without remedy to an injury without a surgeon or balm.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r1.anchor: درشتى ونرمى بهم در بهست ورك زن كه جراح ومرهم نهست

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r2.claim: Moses is told to speak gently to Pharaoh, despite his disbelief, out of regard for the right of the man who raised him; this signals the respect owed to parents.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : أمر الله موسى باللين مع الكافر مراعاة لحق التربية

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r3.claim: As transmitted in al-Iḥyāʾ, al-Hasan says a child may admonish a father while he is calm but should fall silent when the father becomes angry.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r3.anchor: وفي الإحياء سئل الحسن عن الولد كيف يحتسب على والده

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r4.claim: A child must not rebuke or strike a parent harshly; a student differs, since a scholar who does not practice his knowledge has no such inviolability.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r4.anchor: فعلم منه أنه ليس للولد الحسبة على الوالد بالتعنيف والضرب وليس كذلك التلميذ

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r5.claim: Gentleness leaves Pharaoh no excuse to claim that Moses used harsh words in calling him to faith.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r5.anchor: وقيل أمر موسى باللين ليكون حجة على فرعون لئلا يقول أغلظ علي القول

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r6.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r6.claim: Yahya ibn Muʿadh wept, marveling that God treats gently even someone who claims to be God, and asking how much greater His gentleness is toward one who acknowledges Him.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r6.anchor: قرأ رجل عند يحيى بن معاذ رحمه الله هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r7.speaker: الإرشاد
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r7.claim: Al-Irshād says Pharaoh may remember the reminder and desire what the brothers urge, or fear God's punishment; or does not exclude either outcome.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r7.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" لعله يتذكر بما بلغتماه من ذكري

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r8.claim: Some say hope and expectation describe Moses and Aaron, remembrance concerns what is established, and fear what is supposed; fear is awe mixed with reverence and commonly arises from knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الرجاء والطمع راجعان إلى مال موسى وهارون

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r9.claim: The description of fear as especially associated with the learned is linked to the statement that only the learned truly fear God.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r9.anchor: ولذلك خص العلماء بها في قوله {ومن الناس والدوآب والانعام مختلف ألوانه}

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r10.claim: The brothers hope Pharaoh will stop denying truth: he might accept wholeheartedly after reflection, or at least suspect it is true and fear persisting in denial; either is better than stubborn rejection.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r10.anchor: راجيين أن يترك الإصرار على إنكار الحق وتكذيبه إما بأن يتذكر

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r11.claim: Pharaoh remembered and feared only when drowning, when that response could no longer benefit him.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r11.anchor: ولقد تذكر فرعون وخشي حين لم ينفعاه وذلك حين ألجمه الغرق

BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r12.claim: A report says Moses promised Pharaoh lasting youth, rule until death, worldly pleasures until death, and Paradise afterward if he believed; Haman persuaded him that accepting would make a supposed god subject to another, so he refused.
BURSEVI:v5p298#2/r12.anchor: روي أن موسى وعده على قبول الإيمان شبابا لا يهرم

BURSEVI:v5p299/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299/r1.claim: Sending the messengers despite God's knowledge that Pharaoh will not believe establishes proof and removes his excuse; God's custom is to deliver the message before punishment.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r1.anchor: وفائدة إرسالهما إليه مع علمه تعالى بأنه لا يؤمن الزام الحجة

BURSEVI:v5p299/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r2.speaker: بعض أرباب الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v5p299/r2.claim: Some people of spiritual realization distinguish God's prescriptive command from His decree: messengers and heirs serve the prescriptive command, although it may differ from what God decrees.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r2.anchor: قال بعض أرباب الحقيقة : الأمر تكليفي وإرادي والإرادة كثيرا ما تكون مخالفة للأمر

BURSEVI:v5p299/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299/r3.claim: A sinner's fixed identity in divine knowledge has capacity for the duty but no readiness to perform it, which explains disobedience.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r3.anchor: العاصي الثابتة في الحضرة العلمية استعداد التكليف توجه إليه الأمر التكليفي وليس

BURSEVI:v5p299/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299/r4.claim: The point of a command known not to be fulfilled is to distinguish those ready to accept from those not ready, making felicity and misery manifest.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r4.anchor: قلت : فائدته تمييز من له استعداد القبول ممن ليس له استعداد ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p299/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r5.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p299/r5.claim: Hafez's couplet expresses surrender to one's divinely directed course rather than self-reproach.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r5.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
جزء : 5 رقم الصفحة : 388
درين من مكنم سرزنش بخود

BURSEVI:v5p299/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r6.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p299/r6.claim: Al-Baḥr says God's knowledge follows what is known as it is; knowing that Pharaoh freely chooses disbelief does not make belief impossible, so God still commands the two to call him gently.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r6.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : إن الله قد علم كل شيء على ما هو عليه

BURSEVI:v5p299/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p299/r7.claim: Bursevī takes the verse's hope of remembrance or fear as evidence that human capacity affects one's own and others' acts, rejecting al-Ashʿarī's view that people are compelled and their capacity has no effect.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r7.anchor: وفي قوله : {لعله يتذكر أو يخشى} دلالة ظاهرة على أن لقدرة العبد تأثيرا

BURSEVI:v5p299/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p299/r8.speaker: الأشعري
BURSEVI:v5p299/r8.claim: Al-Ashʿarī is cited as denying any effect of human capacity on acts and describing humans as compelled; Bursevī argues the verse contradicts this.
BURSEVI:v5p299/r8.anchor: كما زعم الأشعري حيث قال لا تأثير لقدرة العبد في أفعاله بل هو مجبور

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r4.claim: God commands gentleness because Pharaoh had raised Moses; this honors the claims of those who raise a child and underscores respect for parents.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r4.anchor: أنه عليه السلام كان قد رباه فرعون فأمره أن يخاطبه بالرفق رعاية لتلك الحقوق وهذا تنبيه على نهاية تعظيم حق الأبوين

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r5.claim: Tyrants tend to become more defiant when admonished harshly; the mission seeks benefit rather than greater harm, so gentle speech is appropriate.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r5.anchor: أن من عادة الجبابرة إذا غلظ لهم في الوعظ أن يزدادوا عتوا وتكبرا

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r1.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r1.claim: One account illustrates gentle speech with Moses’ invitation to Pharaoh in 79:18–19 and the message prescribed later in 20:47.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r1.anchor: ما حكى الله تعالى بعضه فقال : { هل لك إلى أن تزكى

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r2.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r2.claim: Another proposed form promised Pharaoh unaging youth, an unlost kingdom, and continued bodily pleasures until death.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r2.anchor: أن تعداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده وملكا لا ينزع منه إلا بالموت وأن يبقى له لذة المطعم والمشرب والمنكح إلى حين موته

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r3.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r3.claim: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār reports hearing that Pharaoh lived 409 years and Moses promised him the same lifespan and Paradise if he obeyed.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r3.anchor: حكى عن عمرو بن دينار قال : بلغني أن فرعون عمر أربعمائة سنة وتسع سنين فقال له موسى عليه السلام : إن أطعتني عمرت مثل ما عمرت فإذا مت فلك الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r4.claim: Another view is that Moses addressed Pharaoh by one of his three kunyas: Abū al-ʿAbbās, Abū al-Walīd, or Abū Murra.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r4.anchor: كنياه وهو من ذوي الكنى الثلاث أبو العباس وأبو الوليد وأبو مرة

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r5.speaker: معترضون
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r5.claim: Critics object that the promised benefits could compel recognition of God, incompatible with moral responsibility; a kunya alone is too slight to exhaust the command, though it could be part of it.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r5.anchor: قيل لو حصلت له هذه الأمور الثلاثة في هذه المدة الطويلة لصار ذلك كالإلجاء إلى معرفة الله تعالى وذلك لا يصح مع التكليف

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r6.claim: “Perhaps” does not imply divine doubt; Moses and Aaron are to speak gently while hoping Pharaoh may reflect or fear.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r6.anchor: ليس المراد أنه تعالى كان شاكا في ذلك لأن ذلك محال

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r7.claim: Hearts persist in truth, persist in falsehood, or suspend judgment; Pharaoh persisted in falsehood, the worst state.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r7.anchor: واعلم أن أحوال القلب ثلاثة . أحدها : الإصرار على الحق

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r8.claim: The gentle call may bring Pharaoh from denial to acknowledgment, or at least make him fear and stop denying, which is better than persistent rejection.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r8.anchor: فيرجع من إنكاره إلى الإقرار بالحق وإن لم ينتقل من الإنكار إلى الإقرار لكنه يحصل في قلبه الخوف فيترك الإنكار

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r9.claim: Rāzī asks how God, knowing Pharaoh cannot believe, could order gentle exhortation that only increases his liability; he compares it to handing a doomed person a knife, then says reason must submit before this mystery.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r9.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التكليف لا يعلم سره إلا الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r10.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r10.claim: Kaʿb reports that the Torah says to speak gently to Pharaoh even though God will harden his heart and he will not believe.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51#2/r10.anchor: يروى عن كعب أنه قال : والذي يحلف به كعب إنه لمكتوب في التوراة : فقولا له قولا لينا وسأقسي قلبه فلا يؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.claim: Gentleness comes first, then firmness once the hearer’s obstinacy appears.
RAZI-FULL:v22p54/r5.anchor: لأن الإنسان إذا ظهر لجاجه فلا بد له من التغليظ
